newsitem.title: MEXICO: Clinton meets with Mexican opposition leaders. [CORRECTED 04:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Clinton meets with Mexican opposition leaders. [CORRECTED 04:50 GMT]

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Tuesday held unprecedented meetings with leaders of Mexican opposition parties that are challenging the 68-year monopoly on power of the ruling Institutional Revoutionary Party (PRI).

On the second day of his state visit to Mexico, Clinton met separately with Felipe Calderon, president of the conservative National Action Party (PAN), and Andres Lopez Obrador, head of the left-leaning Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD).

The first U.S. president to sit down with the Mexican opposition, Clinton said he did so to "support the political reform process in Mexico," noting that he held similar sessions with opposition figures in Russia and Israel.
Mexico, which is holding federal legislative elections on July 6, has seen the dominance of the ruling PRI eroded in recent years.
The conservative PAN currently holds four of the 31 state governorships and the left-leaning PRD is expected to win the first-ever race for the important post of Mexico City mayor.
Both Calderon and Obrador said they raised the thorny topic of immigration at the meetings, which lasted less than half an hour each and took place at Clinton's hotel.

"We expressed our disagreements with the anti-immigrant policy in the United States," Calderon told reporters after, adding that Clinton had assured him the United States would work with the opposition parties if they took power in Mexico.

Clinton was at pains to assuage Mexican sensitivities on immigration and drugs during his appearances throughout the day with Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo. He acknowledged that the U.S. demand for drugs was a major part of the narcotics problem and sought to allay worries about a new U.S. immigration law.
The U.S. president also met briefly on Tuesday evening with Humberto Roque Villanueva, the president of Zedillo's PRI party (corrects name of PRI president).
